walkthrough:
Express the integrand in index form and integrate using the reverse chain rule:
$$\int (3x - 2)^{-3/2}\,dx = \frac{(3x - 2)^{-1/2}}{-\frac{1}{2} \times 3} = -\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3x - 2}}$$

Set up the improper integral with upper limit $b \to \infty$:
$$\int_1^\infty (3x - 2)^{-3/2}\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \left[ -\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3x - 2}} \right]_1^b$$

Evaluate at the upper and lower limits:
$$\lim_{b \to \infty}\left(-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3b - 2}}\right) - \left(-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3(1) - 2}}\right) = 0 - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)$$

State the exact value of the integral:
$$\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{(3x - 2)^{3/2}}\,dx = \frac{2}{3}$$

Square the curve equation to find $y^2$ for the volume of revolution about the $x$-axis:
$$y^2 = \left((3x - 2)^{-3/2}\right)^2 = (3x - 2)^{-3}$$

Integrate $y^2$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$\int (3x - 2)^{-3}\,dx = \frac{(3x - 2)^{-2}}{-2 \times 3} = -\frac{1}{6(3x - 2)^2}$$

Evaluate the definite integral between limits $x = 1$ and $x = 2$:
$$V = \pi \left[ -\frac{1}{6(3x - 2)^2} \right]_1^2 = \pi \left( -\frac{1}{6(4^2)} - \left(-\frac{1}{6(1^2)}\right) \right) = \pi \left( -\frac{1}{96} + \frac{1}{6} \right)$$

hints: Differentiate $y = (3x-2)^{-3/2}$ and substitute $x = 1$ to find tangent gradient $-\frac{9}{2}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = (3x - 2)^{-3/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{3}{2}(3x - 2)^{-5/2} \times 3 = -\frac{9}{2(3x - 2)^{5/2}}$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient and perpendicular normal gradient at $(1, 1)$:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{9}{2(1)^{5/2}} = -\frac{9}{2}$$
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{-\frac{9}{2}} = \frac{2}{9}$$

Form the equation of the normal line through $(1, 1)$:
$$y - 1 = \frac{2}{9}(x - 1) \implies y = \frac{2}{9}x + \frac{7}{9}$$
